title: Settings Soup refuses at load
description: Settings Soup refuses when the config loads: the v0.76.0 refusals, the 31 staged fields and two deprecated config values refused since v0.77.0, and the never-applied settings v0.77.0 added, each with what to change.

headings.title: How a config loads at v0.77.0
Variants and modes that never ran
Keys that are still unread and not refused
What soup doctor --config does and does not check

blocks.html:
Settings Soup refuses at load

A soup.yaml used to be able to ask for one thing and train another: the schema accepted the setting, a validator checked its range, and for most settings nothing on the path it named ever read it (for a few, listed below, what read it did the wrong thing). v0.76.0 refused the settings that never took effect and warned about the ones it still tolerated. v0.77.0 refuses those too, and fourteen of the fifteen settings that, in upstream's list, v0.76 accepted without a word (the fifteenth, a KTO row with a malformed label, is dropped at data load with a reason). This page is the reference for what the load does at v0.77.0: how it decides, the refusals grouped by what they touch with the start of each message and what to change (rows that differ only by task or backend are merged), the 31 staged fields, the deprecated values, and the keys that are still unread but not refused.

Unknown keys have refused the load since v0.75.0, and that has not changed. Upstream publishes no count of the other refusals, so neither does this page.

Run that on every config that loaded on an older release before you train with v0.77.0. It loads the file with the same rules as soup train, prints the error if the load is refused, and exits 2. Unknown keys are reported together, but a refusal that spans several fields prints only the first one it hits, so fix that setting and run the command again until it prints no error.

How a config loads at v0.77.0

soup train and the other commands that build a config from a soup.yaml (soup doctor --config, soup bench, soup cost, soup profile, soup sweep, soup recipes verify --config, and the --config forms of some soup eval and soup data commands) call one loader. It does these things in this order:

  1. The file is read under limits (since v0.76.1, #1827). Every YAML file Soup reads goes through one loader. Nesting is limited to 100 levels, and the document's top-level mapping counts as the first, so 99 levels of brackets under a top-level key is the deepest structure that loads; expansion is limited to one node per source byte plus 10,000 for anchors, aliases and merge keys, with merge keys chained at most 100 levels; and a soup.yaml may be at most 1 MiB. A file over a limit, a directory, a file the system will not let Soup read, bytes that are not UTF-8 and a file that is not valid YAML (a syntax error, or a value YAML cannot build, such as a date that does not exist) each stop the load with one line that names the file and the problem, before any key is checked, for example Config file soup.yaml is larger than 1048576 bytes; refusing, Config file soup.yaml nests collections more than 100 levels deep; refusing, Config file soup.yaml expands to more than N nodes from M bytes of YAML; refusing, Config file soup.yaml is not valid YAML: <problem> (line L, column C), Config file soup.yaml is not valid UTF-8: ... and Config file soup.yaml is a directory, not a file. soup train exits 1 and soup doctor --config exits 2. Through v0.76.0 there was no size, nesting or expansion limit, and a syntax error printed the parser's own multi-line message. A hand-written config is kilobytes; what the limits stop is a generated file, or a few hundred bytes of anchors and aliases that describe a structure many times larger.
  2. The file must be a YAML mapping. An empty file prints Config file is empty and a list or a bare value prints Config must be a YAML mapping, got list; soup train exits 1 on both and soup doctor --config exits 2.
  3. An unknown key refuses the load. The message is unknown config key 'x' - did you mean 'y'? Refused. When no key is close, it names the key and suggests nothing. Typos such as early_stopp_patience land here, and they are checked before anything else: nothing else is reported until the unknown keys are gone.
  4. The schema validates the values and the combinations. A value out of range, a key that needs another key, a deprecated value and every refusal in the tables below come from this step. A failure prints Config validation error: and one indented line per problem. A refusal of one field reads training -> optimizer: <message>; a refusal that spans several fields prints its message alone, or after training: or data: when it comes from that section's own check. Since v0.77.0 the terminal no longer prints Pydantic's Value error, prefix in front of a message; the loader that the API and the Web UI use (load_config_from_string) raises a ValueError whose text keeps it.
  5. A staged field set away from its default refuses the load (since v0.77.0; v0.76 warned). Each prints <section>.<name> is accepted but read by nothing; refused as of v0.77. Delete the line., one line per field, ahead of every other error in the same report. When a staged field's own check fails as well (for example training.grace_codebook: true without a size and a dimension, or data.video_fps on a format that is not video), only the staged line is shown, so no message asks you to fix a line that the next load refuses anyway. See The 31 staged fields.

Since v0.77.0 the loader prints no warning of its own. soup train still prints a Note: after the load for five keys that are set but not enforced (see Keys that are still unread and not refused).

Outcomesoup doctor --configsoup train
Refused (a file over a read limit, unreadable or not valid YAML; an unknown key; a staged field; a deprecated value; a value or combination below)prints the error, then Config could not be loaded (see above)., exits 2prints Config validation error: (or the read-limit line) and exits 1, before it imports the training stack
Loadsexits 0trains

soup recipes verify --config exits 3 on a refused config (Config does not parse: ...). soup plan and soup apply are the exception to the table: they read the YAML under the read limits and run the unknown-key check, not the schema validators, so soup plan --config writes a plan for a config that soup train refuses. The other YAML readers apply the same nesting and expansion limits with their own size caps, and report a refusal through their own handlers: soup plan and soup apply exit 2 on a limit and 1 on a syntax error, soup eval gate exits 3 on a suite over a limit and 1 on a syntax error (soup train --gate exits 1 on either), and soup ship --config reads up to 4 MiB and exits 3. Configuration lists the caps and Exit codes the codes.

Here is a config that loaded on v0.76 with two warnings and is refused at v0.77.0. The keys are real, they validate, and nothing reads them (this fence shows a refusal on purpose):

blocks.code:
base: org/model
task: sft
data:
  train: ./data.jsonl
training:
  early_stop_patience: 3
  lr_groups:
    - pattern: ".*lora_A.*"
      lr: 0.001

Config validation error:

  training.lr_groups is accepted but read by nothing; refused as of v0.77. Delete the line.
  training.early_stop_patience is accepted but read by nothing; refused as of v0.77. Delete the line.

blocks.html:
soup train --config exits 1 on it and soup doctor --config exits 2. A field is refused only when its value differs from the schema default, so early_stop_patience: 2 loads and 3 is refused. Rich wraps these lines to the width of your terminal.

What to do with a refusal. Remove the key, or change it as the message says. Deleting the key is the fix. For a staged field it changes no result, because none of them changed what a run did. For most other rows below, the setting was not read, or the run stopped after the model had loaded. A few keys are different: on v0.75, training.use_longlora: true, training.ebft_variant and training.quantization_aware: true WERE applied, wrongly, and Re-run this on the v0.76.0 release page lists them; the v0.77.0 ones (for example ReLoRA on a loss with a frozen reference, and LLaMA Pro with a LoRA rank) are on the v0.77.0 release page. Renaming a key does nothing useful: these settings were read or ignored, not misspelled. A config that has to load on both v0.76 and v0.77 needs the key removed. Configs Soup itself wrote on v0.75 or earlier (soup autopilot output and run-config dumps) can carry data.remove_unused_columns: true or training.quantization: 4bit on a task that never quantizes; delete those lines.

Settings that are refused

Each row was checked against the loader and the validators at the v0.77.0 tag, and the messages were probed on the v0.77.0 binary. The third column is the exact start of the message, which always goes on to say what to change; the fourth column is that advice in short. Pull request numbers are upstream's. Where one setting is refused in several task or backend combinations the rows are merged. Rows and conditions new in v0.77.0 say so.

Variants and modes that never ran

training.gdpo_variantany value (#1309)training.gdpo_variant is refused (#1309): supported TRL versions do not expose the dpo_loss hook, so this setting was accepted but ignored.Remove it and use plain task: dpo

training.rope_scaling_typelongrope (#1239)training.rope_scaling_type='longrope' is refused (#1239): it cannot extend any checkpoint.Choose another rope_scaling_type

Optimizers

The allowlist is 24 names (v0.76.0 cut it from 32). The checks apply to training.optimizer (#1269, #1283).

SettingRefused whenMessage beginsWhat to change
training.optimizeradam_mini, adamw_apex_fused, ao_adamw_4bit, ao_adamw_8bit, ao_adamw_fp8, badam, came_pytorch or dionoptimizer='badam' is no longer supported: transformers 5.x rejects it in TrainingArguments after the model has loaded, so Soup refuses it at config load instead.Use adamw_torch, adamw_torch_fused, adamw_bnb_8bit, adafactor or another name from the 24-name allowlist
training.optimizermuon or adamw_hf on any backend except mlxtraining.optimizer='muon' only works on backend: mlx (the MLX backend builds it itself);Switch to backend: mlx, or use a supported optimizer

Refused later than config load

soup train --dry-run and soup doctor --config pass these, because the check needs the model or the trainer:

  • a LoRA target on the streamed embed_tokens or lm_head of an untied checkpoint, whatever its spelling, refused when the streamed model is built and before a streaming buffer is allocated (training.stream_layers does not yet support a LoRA target on the streamed lm_head of an untied checkpoint:, #2082). On a tied checkpoint it trains and saves. Through v0.76.1 this was a config-load check on the literal names only.
  • training.freeze_layers or freeze_ratio under LoRA with a target peft cannot restrict by layer: a string lora.target_modules (a regular expression, all-linear, or what auto resolves to on some architectures), lora.target_parameters, lora.use_vera, a list naming a module outside the decoder layers, or a plan that freezes every layer, refused when the model is built (training.freeze_layers / training.freeze_ratio cannot currently be combined with a string training.lora.target_modules, #2145).
  • a preference_loss_weights blend with a dpo or ipo term under a simpo or orpo primary, together with lora.init_strategy pissa, olora or loftq, refused at trainer setup before the model loads (#1828). The same blend with relora_steps is refused at config load instead (#1891, the relora_steps row above). A bco term in a blend is still refused at trainer setup.
  • task: ppo with reward_hack_detector, reward_hack_mitigation or echo_trap_enabled, refused when the trainer is built on trl's experimental PPOTrainer, before the model loads (task: ppo itself still runs; the refusal is for the flags PPO cannot feed).
  • on a layer-streamed run, at trainer setup: stream_expert_layout: per_expert on a base that is not deepseek_v3; a base checkpoint that is itself quantized (GPTQ, AWQ, bitsandbytes, compressed-tensors and the like, or an FP8 format other than DeepSeek-V3's block FP8), refused by name before the shard cache is written (#2103, #2061); a Kimi K2 config that the guard does not admit (#2107); and, under stream_loss_chunk, a trainable output head or a model that changes its logits after the head.
  • on backend: mlx, when the trainer starts: an SFT training split smaller than batch_size, eval_steps with a validation split that comes out empty, DPO, ORPO or SimPO with fewer pairs than batch_size once unusable rows are skipped, and KTO with fewer than 2 rows.

soup train --dry-run validates the config and the data and, for a run that is not layer-streamed and has a GPU whose memory it can read, the hardware-fit check; it does not run the layer-streaming VRAM pre-flight, which runs at trainer setup.

Keys that are still unread and not refused

Not every key that nothing reads is in the staged table, and these load. House phrasing for them: accepted by the schema, but nothing in v0.77.0 reads it. Upstream names no release for refusing them.

  • Four parent switches and one threshold: training.forgetting_detection, training.checkpoint_intelligence, training.early_stop_on_regression, training.convergence_detection (when true) and training.forgetting_threshold (when it differs from the default). soup train prints a Note: after the load that they are set but not enforced during training; soup doctor --config does not print it. Use --gate <suite.yaml> for a live eval gate, or run soup eval or soup diagnose after training.
  • training.warmup_auto. It loads in silence. soup autopilot writes it into the config it generates, and nothing that trains reads it.
  • training.load_in_16bit, training.unsloth_bnb_4bit and training.llm_int8 are aliases that the schema rewrites, not separate settings.

training.packing_cross_doc_attn_mask is not one of them: it is refused at load, as before.

Upstream tracks the class as #1814, still open at v0.77.0: its guard test lists the staged fields plus warmup_auto and forgetting_threshold among the declared fields that nothing consumes. Data pipeline pro covers the video and image fields.

What soup doctor --config does and does not check

soup doctor --config soup.yaml loads the file with the loader described above. So, on every task and backend, it reports unknown keys (all of them together; a config that has one stops there, before the staged fields are checked), then the staged fields and deprecated values (together, ahead of the rest), and the refusals on this page that happen at config load. It does not list every refusal in one run: it stops at the first cross-field refusal it hits, and a refusal of one data field can hide a cross-field one, so fix what it names and run it again until it prints no error. A refused config exits 2 and a config that loads exits 0. Since v0.77.0 it no longer prints All checks passed! above a refusal (#2106); the system, GPU and dependency tables still print first, and the config error follows them.

After a successful load it prints a Config check section: a table of settings known to be unread on a combination of task, backend and modality that upstream has reviewed. At v0.77.0 there are eight: sft on backend: mlx (12 settings); dpo, orpo, simpo and kto on backend: mlx (9 each); sft on backend: unsloth (none, because its unread settings are refused at load instead); and sft on the transformers backend with a vision or an audio modality (data.mask_history, one each). A setting refused at load never reaches the table. For every other combination it prints None of the 0 setting(s) known to be unread on task=<task> backend=<backend> is switched on in this config. That line means "not reviewed", not an all-clear, and the reviewed combinations print the same form with their own count. Upstream tracks this as #1815.

soup plan and soup apply read the YAML under the read limits (a file over one exits 2) and with the unknown-key check only (an unknown key exits 1), not with the schema validators, so soup plan --config writes a plan for a config with a staged field or training.quantization_aware: true, which soup doctor --config and soup train refuse; use soup doctor --config as the check. See Refused later than config load for what no load-time check can see, MLX honours its config for how the MLX table started, and Exit codes for the other commands' codes.
